key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict frequency-dependent dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules from molecular structure, capturing both dispersive and absorptive optical behavior.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster screening of photoactive organic molecules for optoelectronic and organic photovoltaic device design, reducing reliance on expensive TD-DFT calculations.
method: Equivariant GNN maps 3D molecular geometry and UV-vis information to complex-valued, frequency-dependent polarizability tensors.
Model learns tensor shape and magnitude across optical frequencies, including real and imaginary components.
Predictions are fed into device-level optical simulations to estimate charge-carrier generation rates.
evidence_signal: The model reproduces dynamic polarizability features on QM9 and Harvard OPV datasets, and downstream optical simulations match TD-DFT-based charge generation with R² = 0.94.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of training data, so unusual chemistries or excitation regimes may still require TD-DFT validation.
paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
